claims.text: Overall Green Flood in Afghanistan from 19 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC to 21 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC. Flood can have a low humanitarian impact based on the magnitude, exposed population and vulnerability. At least 20 people were killed, around 80 others injured, and more than 100 remain missing, in Nuristan Province following flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall.

UN News (22 July 2026): flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall on 20 July have killed at least 26 people across eastern Afghanistan, including 23 in Nuristan province, where homes, markets and roads were swept away, with the worst devastation in Parun City (7 houses completely destroyed, 23 partially damaged, 70 shops and 11 hotels damaged, 40 vehicles lost). The floods also killed three Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing with Pakistan and injured nine others there. OCHA said the immediate priority is to save lives and reach people who may still be missing or injured, and warned that casualty figures could rise as more information becomes available; UNICEF and partners are setting up a field clinic in Parun for trauma care.

OCHA Flash Update #2: Flooding in Eastern Afghanistan (22-23 July 2026): in Parun City, Nuristan Province, local authorities report 23 killed, 5 missing (down from over 100) and 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor). At the Torkham transit camp in Nangarhar, 3 Afghan refugees were killed and 9 injured (unchanged). One additional death is reported in Maidan Wardak province (Sayedabad District). The response has moved from immediate search and rescue and emergency life-saving assistance towards a broader, multi-sector response addressing shelter, health, food, WASH, protection, livelihoods and planning to address early recovery needs.

OCHA Flash Update #3: Flooding in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Afghanistan (as of 28 July 2026): in Laghman Province, three people were killed and four others injured, with 187 families affected and 183 houses damaged or destroyed; approximately 800 acres of seasonal crops and around 310 livestock were also reportedly lost or damaged. Nuristan Province remains the most severely affected area; the completed inter-agency needs assessment in Parun district identified 120 families eligible for humanitarian assistance, of which the first 92 have already received assistance. The Shelter/NFI cluster reports 1,168 families have been affected across 14 provinces, including 234 houses completely destroyed and 930 houses damaged. Needs assessments in Maidan Wardak and Panjshir are expected to commence shortly.

published.description: Torrential monsoon rains triggered flash floods in Afghanistan's eastern Nuristan province beginning around 19 July 2026, striking the provincial capital Parun and surrounding villages, and also killed Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing. GDACS assessed the event as an overall Green alert for low humanitarian impact. OCHA's Flash Update #2 (23 July 2026) reported the confirmed death toll had held near 27 across eastern Afghanistan while the number of people missing in Nuristan had fallen sharply from over 100 to 5. OCHA's Flash Update #3 (as of 28 July 2026) shows the response has now broadened geographically to Central, Eastern and Southeastern Afghanistan, with new flood-related casualties confirmed in Laghman Province (3 killed, 4 injured, 187 families affected) in addition to the original Nuristan/Torkham/Maidan Wardak toll. Nuristan remains the most severely affected area, where a completed inter-agency needs assessment in Parun district identified 120 families eligible for assistance; across the now-widened 14-province response, the Shelter/NFI cluster reports 1,168 families affected, including 234 houses destroyed and 930 damaged. No authoritative source has declared the event resolved.

impact.summary: OCHA's Flash Update #2 (23 July 2026) reported 23 people killed and 5 still missing (down from 100+) in Nuristan Province, with 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor) there; the 3 Afghan refugees killed and 9 injured at the Torkham border transit camp and 1 additional death in Maidan Wardak province were unchanged — a combined toll of 27 confirmed deaths across eastern Afghanistan. OCHA's Flash Update #3 (as of 28 July 2026) broadens the response to Central, Eastern and Southeastern Afghanistan and reports 3 further deaths and 4 injuries in Laghman Province (187 families affected, 183 houses damaged/destroyed), bringing the combined confirmed death toll to at least 30. Nuristan remains the most severely affected area, with a completed inter-agency needs assessment in Parun district identifying 120 families eligible for assistance (92 already assisted); the Shelter/NFI cluster now reports 1,168 families affected across 14 provinces (234 houses destroyed, 930 damaged). No authoritative source has declared the event resolved. Algeria's interior ministry reported six deaths from the wildfires, and authorities reported more than 100 people hospitalised in the town of Seraidi and about 150 homes damaged there.

Algeria's interior ministry registered six deaths in relation to the fires affecting multiple provinces during this period; four people were arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting fires.

GDACS's event report for a third concurrent Green-alert forest fire in Algeria, now at episode 5 covering a 21-24 July 2026 window, cites about 13,388 hectares burned, assessed as low humanitarian impact based on burned area and affected population. Thermal-anomaly detections continue to be recorded as of 24 July 2026.

Over the last 24 hours, the Ministry of the Interior, Local Authorities and Transport confirmed six fatalities linked to the wildfires. In Seraïdi, Annaba, more than 100 patients were evacuated from a rehabilitation hospital, while approximately 150 homes were affected or threatened. Preventive evacuations were also carried out in several localities, including El Tarf, Béjaïa, Guelma and Bouira.

Flash Update #2 (dated 11 July 2026, published 13 July) reports that 10 districts have been affected, more than 1.07 million people have been impacted, over 36,000 people remain temporarily displaced, and 26 casualties have been reported.

Situation Report #1 (dated 13 July 2026, published 14 July) reports 51 reported fatalities and more than 1.11 million people affected across 10 districts (Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Khagrachhari, Rangamati, Moulvibazar, Sunamganj, Habiganj, Sylhet and Cumilla), with more than 38,000 people staying in over 1,000 evacuation shelters as of 12 July, and significant damage to homes, water systems, roads, bridges and public infrastructure.

Oxfam situation report on the Bangladesh flash floods (15 July 2026): 1.11 million people affected across 10 districts, 53 fatalities and 39 injuries reported as of 15 July; Chattogram district was hardest-hit, with Chattogram city recording 412.3mm of rain in 24 hours, the highest single-day July rainfall in 42 years.

BDRCS/IFRC nationwide situation report (14 July 2026): 1,074,534 people affected (NAWG figure) across 10 districts, about 38,500 people temporarily displaced (MoDMR figure) across 1,000+ shelters, 51 deaths, 267,918 households stranded, including 15 Rohingya refugee deaths reported by UNHCR among the Cox's Bazar camp toll.

BDRCS/IFRC nationwide situation report (posted 20 Jul 2026, originally published 19 Jul 2026): NAWG estimates 1,116,174 people affected across 10 districts (up from 1,074,534). MoDMR reports ~38,500 people temporarily displaced across 1,000+ shelters and 267,918 households stranded/isolated across seven districts (unchanged). At least 59 people have died nationwide (up from 53/51). In Cox's Bazar's 33 Rohingya refugee camps, flooding/landslides affected 28,000+ people, damaged 3,100+ shelters, and displaced 4,700+ individuals; UNHCR has confirmed 15 deaths among Rohingya refugees. As of 16 July only the Kushiyara River remained above danger level (at Markuli, Sunamganj and Fenchuganj, Sylhet), and water levels in the Surma (Sylhet/Sunamganj) and the Teesta, Dharla and Dudhkumar rivers (Rangpur Division) were falling.

Bangladesh Red Crescent Society Situation Report 4: Monsoon Flood & Landslide Response (posted 20 Jul 2026, originally published 17 Jul 2026), covering Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari, Cumilla, Moulvibazar, Habiganj, Sunamganj and Sylhet. As of 16 July 9:00 AM, only the Kushiyara River remained above danger level (Markuli/Sunamganj and Fenchuganj/Sylhet stations); the Someshwari River at Kalmakanda had receded below danger level; Surma river conditions in Sylhet/Sunamganj were expected to improve within 24 hours; Teesta, Dharla and Dudhkumar river levels in Rangpur Division were falling and projected to fall further. BDRCS Emergency Operations Centre remains active.

Oxfam/CODEC Rapid Needs Assessment (RNA) Report on the Bangladesh Flash Flood 2026 (posted 21 Jul 2026): deep-dive assessment of Satkania and Banshkhali upazilas (Chattogram Division) found 360,000+ people affected in Satkania and 110,000+ in Banshkhali; 90-95% of surveyed households reported partial/complete loss of belongings; 92% of drinking water sources damaged/contaminated (94% in Banshkhali lacking safe water); all assessed latrines submerged; 90% of households reported insufficient food access and 59% reported signs of malnutrition.

UN Resident Coordinator's Office Bangladesh Situation Report #2 (dated 23 July 2026, data as of 22 July) reports approximately 1.28 million people affected across seven of the hardest-hit districts, 59 deaths, 74,479 houses damaged or destroyed, and about 436,000 people assessed as requiring humanitarian assistance; food, cash, health, protection, shelter and WASH assistance activities remain active, with continued risk flagged from forecast heavy rainfall in affected districts.

published.description: Monsoon-triggered flash floods, riverine flooding and landslides across Chattogram Division and adjoining south-eastern/north-eastern Bangladesh districts (including Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari, Cumilla, Moulvibazar, Habiganj, and, as the risk shifted north, Sylhet, Sunamganj and Rangpur), ongoing since early July 2026. Response activities (food, cash, health, shelter, protection and WASH assistance) remain active, with continued risk flagged from forecast heavy rainfall; no authoritative source has declared the event resolved or contained.

As of 17 July 2026, Uganda reported 20 confirmed cases including two deaths in imported cases plus one probable case resulting in death. WHO assessed the risk as very high nationally in DRC due to ongoing transmission and expansion into new health zones, high in Uganda due to confirmed cross-border spread, high for countries sharing land borders with the affected countries, and low for the rest of the African region and globally.

Aid officials say the true number of fatalities is likely much higher, and the disease is expected to spread further as the rainy season sets in, particularly among people who have fled towns and rural areas in North Kordofan.

WHO delivered 8.5 tonnes of medical supplies to Kadugli and Dilling, South Kordofan — its first shipment there since December 2024 — and UNICEF delivered health supplies to El Fula, West Kordofan, serving about 429,000 people.

published.description: A tropical disturbance east-southeast of the Marianas organized into Tropical Depression 09W on 1 July 2026 and was named Bavi as a tropical storm on 2 July. Bavi underwent rapid intensification and reached Category 5 super typhoon strength by 4 July with sustained winds near 287 km/h, prompting GDACS to issue an overall Red alert as the storm tracked through Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. After passing near Rota, the storm continued west, entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility on 8 July (locally named Inday), tracked across Taiwan and Japan's Ryukyu Islands, and made landfall in Zhejiang Province, eastern China, on 11 July before weakening over land.

impact.summary: Super Typhoon Bavi (locally named Inday in the Philippines) made landfall in Zhejiang Province, eastern China, at 23:20 local time on 11 July 2026, after peaking at Category 5 strength (287 km/h sustained winds) near Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands on 4-6 July. GDACS's event report (current as of 12 July 2026) keeps the overall alert at Red for an event window of 01 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC to 11 Jul 2026 18:00 UTC, with a population of 35.3 million exposed to Category 1 (120 km/h) or higher winds; the current alert's urgency status is now 'Past', consistent with the storm weakening after landfall. GDACS's report does not list a confirmed fatality count for the event; Philippine media reported at least 18-19 deaths from landslides and heavy rain on Mindanao, and China evacuated more than 1.7 million people in Zhejiang ahead of landfall, though neither figure comes from an allowlisted authoritative source.

published.description: Tropical Cyclone NOUL-26 (named Kiyapo in the Philippines, Hongxia in China) tracked across the northern Philippines and the South China Sea in late July 2026 before making a second landfall in Guangdong province, southern China, around 26 July 2026. GDACS assessed an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, with about 11.9 million people exposed to Category 1 or higher wind speeds across the Philippines and China, maximum sustained winds of 157 km/h (Category 2 equivalent, per JTWC data), and a maximum storm surge of 1.6 metres recorded on 25 July 2026. GDACS's event window closed at 26 July 2026 00:00 UTC with the alert's urgency status marked "Past" and no episode updates since; no allowlisted authoritative source has published a confirmed death toll, injury count, or evacuation figure for this storm, and with the cyclone dissipated and no further GDACS activity for five days, the event is assessed as resolved.

claims.text: On 25 June 2026 a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck 16 km SW of Moron in northern Venezuela, west of Caracas.

OCHA's Situation Report #22 (15 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,829 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

OCHA's Situation Report #23 (16 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,930 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes, with more than 1,308 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. The additional appeal was raised to US$299 million, still targeting 1.3 million people over six months. EU Commissioner for Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib conducted a field visit to La Guaira together with the UN Humanitarian Coordinator to review response efforts.

OCHA's Situation Report #24 (17 July 2026, 8:00 pm) states that, twenty-three days since the earthquakes, authorities report an official toll of 5,069 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,331 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report #26 (19 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 5,208 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,388 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes. An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months, on top of the US$632 million 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan.

Situation Report No. 28, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 21 July 2026, Time: 9:00 pm. Authorities report 1,405 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,346 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. The US$299 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan complements the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan, increasing the target population from 5.5 million to 6.2 million people and raising total funding requirements from US$632 million to US$931 million.

Situation Report No. 30, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 23 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm. Authorities report 1,463 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,398 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. Starting with this edition, the report will be published on a weekly basis. The next edition will be released on 30 July.

OCHA Situation Report #31, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 31 July 2026, 5:00 pm: authorities report 1,500 aftershocks since the 24 June doublet earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). Official toll: 5,546 people dead and 16,740 injured; 17,907 people lost their homes. As of 30 July, 207,700 people (54% women and girls) have accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance. The additional US$299 million appeal remains in place, complementing the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan for combined requirements of US$931 million targeting 6.2 million people, of whom 1.3 million are earthquake-affected. The report continues to be published weekly.
Re-checked 2 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026) remains the latest in its series; no Situation Report #32 has been published as of 2 August 2026, and figures are unchanged.
The USGS is assessing earthquake-triggered landslide hazards generated by the 2026 Venezuela earthquake sequence.

As of 1 July 2026, nearly 2,000 deaths have been confirmed and more than 6,400 people rescued; 1.8 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance including 680,000 children across six affected states, with around 1,000 buildings and over 400 schools damaged and more than 600 aftershocks recorded since the initial quakes.

OCHA's Situation Report #14 (07 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,685 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes. Authorities also reported that approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and that more than 1,076 aftershocks have been recorded, with at least seven (7) states impacted and La Guaira remaining the most affected state.

OCHA's Situation Report #15 (08 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,811 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and more than 1,100 aftershocks have been recorded. An additional appeal for US$296 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

A first assessment by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) estimates direct physical damage to housing and infrastructure at some $37 billion, comprising $24 billion in damage to buildings and another $13 billion in infrastructure; at least 79 transitional camps have opened in stadiums and sports centres, hosting displaced residents and providing aid.

OCHA's Situation Report #18 (11 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that seventeen days after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,333 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency; 1,171 aftershocks have been recorded, 17,907 people remain without housing, and 315 of those who died have yet to be identified. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher concluded his four-day visit to the country and called for sustained international support for the Humanitarian Response Plan; an additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report No. 20 (13 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that, nineteen days since the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,561 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency, with more than 1,254 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. Authorities report at least 856 affected buildings, including 190 that have collapsed. The response continues with 107 transitional camps supporting affected populations, with a capacity of 25,064 people and a current occupancy of 20,231 people. A preliminary UNDP estimate indicates direct physical damage of US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 percent of GDP, alongside the earlier UNDRR estimate of approximately US$37 billion. The Government of Venezuela announced the creation of an initial reconstruction fund equivalent to US$200 million.

OCHA's Situation Report #21 (14 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,734 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

published.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck northern Venezuela west of Caracas on 25 June 2026, 39 seconds after a magnitude 7.2 foreshock in the same sequence. The USGS assessed that high casualties and widespread damage are probable, and the national government of Venezuela declared a state of emergency. Five weeks on, the confirmed death toll has continued to climb past 5,540, and the UN humanitarian response has shifted toward a longer-term, multi-month recovery phase, with combined funding requirements exceeding $900 million.

impact.summary: As of OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026, 5:00 pm), 37 days after the 24 June doublet quakes, the official toll stands at 5,546 dead and 16,740 injured (up from 5,398 dead in SitRep #30 eight days earlier), with 1,500 aftershocks recorded (up from 1,463) and 17,907 people who lost their homes. As of 30 July, 207,700 people (54% women/girls) had accessed essential services or humanitarian assistance. Funding and targeting figures are unchanged: the combined 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan plus the US$299 million addendum still totals US$931 million in requirements, targeting 6.2 million people, of whom 1.3 million are earthquake-affected. OCHA continues weekly situation reports, consistent with a response shifting toward recovery rather than acute emergency. Earlier assessments put direct physical damage at $37 billion (UNDRR) and $6.7 billion / 6% of GDP (UNDP). Re-checked 2 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026) remains the latest in its series; no Situation Report #32 has been published as of 2 August 2026, and figures are unchanged.

claims.text: OCHA's oPt Humanitarian Situation Report (23 July 2026) states: 'Fatalities linked to settler attacks in 2026 have already surpassed the total recorded during all of 2025, with 18 Palestinians killed as of 20 July compared with 17 throughout 2025,' and 'about 90 Palestinians were displaced by demolitions and settler attacks during the reporting period, most following a large-scale demolition carried out by Israeli authorities in a Bedouin community in Qalqiliya governorate.'

Human Rights Watch (hosted on ReliefWeb): 'Two Israeli settler attacks on Tal village near Nablus in the West Bank on July 24, 2026, resulted in the killing of four Palestinians and two Israelis... The July 24 killings in Tal bring the Palestinian death toll in the occupied West Bank since July 19 to 10.' The incident triggered a wave of settler reprisal attacks on nearby Palestinian villages and the Israeli government's announcement of a 'major counterterrorism operation.'

Per the same ReliefWeb-hosted Human Rights Watch report: 'As of July 19, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026, at least 13 by settlers. OCHA reported that as of July 15, 20 Israelis had been injured in 2026 in the West Bank.'

UN News, citing OHCHR and OCHA (29 July 2026): 'As of 24 July, the agency reports that 76 Palestinians and one Israeli have died this year in settler attacks... Since Friday, eight Palestinians, including a boy, and two members of the Israeli military have also been killed in the region.' 'The number of settler attacks has increased each year since 2023... rising to 1,835 last year.' 'There were about 190 attacks per month in the first four months of 2026, putting the West Bank on a trajectory to reach more than 2,000 attacks by the end of the year.' 'Nearly 700 Palestinians in nine communities in the West Bank were displaced as a result of settler attacks in the first four months of 2026.'

UN News (29 July 2026), citing OHCHR and OCHA: 'As of 24 July, the agency reports that 76 Palestinians and one Israeli have died this year in settler attacks... Since Friday, eight Palestinians, including a boy, and two members of the Israeli military have also been killed in the region.' The article describes West Bank settler violence as having hit an 'all-time high.' It also reconfirms OCHA's separate figure that 18 Palestinians died in 2026 as of 20 July in attacks involving settlers (12 by settlers, 3 by Israeli forces, 3 disputed responsibility), and repeats the 'nearly 700 Palestinians across nine communities' displacement figure for the first four months of 2026.

published.description: A sharp escalation of Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank culminated on 24 July 2026 when Israeli settlers carried out two attacks on Tal village near Nablus, leaving four Palestinians (two brothers and two cousins from the Ramadan family) and two Israelis dead, and triggering a wave of settler reprisal attacks on nearby Palestinian villages, mosque burnings, and an Israeli government-announced 'major counterterrorism operation.' The attack capped a week of escalating violence: OCHA reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026 as of 19 July (at least 13 by settlers), rising to about 10 Palestinian deaths in the week since 19 July alone, while fatalities linked specifically to settler attacks in 2026 (18 as of 20 July) had already surpassed the full-year 2025 total of 17. A newer OHCHR figure reported via UN News on 29 July 2026 puts settler-attack fatalities substantially higher — 76 Palestinians and 1 Israeli killed in settler attacks so far in 2026 as of 24 July, on a trajectory to exceed 2,000 settler attacks for the year (up from 1,835 in 2025), with nearly 700 Palestinians displaced across nine West Bank communities in the first four months of 2026 alone. The same UN News report states that, since 24 July, a further eight Palestinians (including a child) and two Israeli military members have been killed, describing West Bank settler violence as having hit an 'all-time high.' This OHCHR count and OCHA's 18-killed figure appear to use different methodologies or scopes and have not been reconciled by an authoritative source. The violence is occurring amid a fragile Gaza ceasefire and continued deterioration of humanitarian conditions across the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

impact.summary: The 24 July settler attacks on Tal village near Nablus killed 4 Palestinians and 2 Israelis and brought the West Bank Palestinian death toll since 19 July to 10 (per Human Rights Watch, hosted on ReliefWeb). OCHA reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026 as of 19 July (at least 13 by settlers) and 20 Israelis injured in 2026 as of 15 July. A newer OHCHR figure reported via UN News (29 July 2026) puts 2026 settler-attack fatalities as of 24 July at 76 Palestinians and 1 Israeli, alongside about 190 settler attacks per month in the first four months of 2026 (on pace to exceed 2,000 for the year, up from 1,835 in 2025) and nearly 700 Palestinians displaced across nine communities in that four-month window. The same UN News report (29 July 2026) states that, since 24 July, a further eight Palestinians (including a child) and two Israeli military members have been killed, and describes West Bank settler violence as having reached an 'all-time high.' The OHCHR and OCHA settler-attack death tolls have not been reconciled by an authoritative source.
